records.title: OpenAI · seven eighths
records.method: OpenAI’s quasi-Riemann framework establishes the 7/8 boundary. The original pinned proof has now been rebuilt and checked directly.
records.verification_note: The original proof passed local verification with Palomar’s mechanical checker: Comparator compared the exact statements and their definitions, then con-ron, NanoDa and Lean’s fresh kernel accepted the exported proofs. All-Dirichlet, zeta and finite-order Eisenstein Hecke targets were checked, with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound allowed. This is a local check; Palomar registration and editorial review are separate.

records.title: Argonaut · perturbed boundary
records.method: Refinement of the OpenAI framework to 3499999/4000000. Authors report Lean and native Comparator verification; our independent verification is pending.
records.verification_note: Authors report Lean and native Comparator verification. We have inspected sources but have not independently reproduced the complete proof check. This is a verification status, not a claim that the proof is defective.

records.title: Baiying Liu · optimized parameters
records.method: Optimizes b and ℓ in the OpenAI argument. The exact boundary is algebraic. The plotted rational is a certified upper endpoint less than 10⁻³⁰ above it, used only for rendering.
records.verification_note: The author reports a Lean formalization. We have not independently reproduced it. No Liu proof code is redistributed in this repository.

records.title: Nielstron · compressed rational refinement
records.method: Compresses the ProofCouncil Lean development, then tightens its exact rational certificate and slack budgets. The all-Dirichlet, zeta and finite-order Eisenstein Hecke targets compile at the smaller rational boundary. Final QRH source tokens decrease from 294,019 to 251,464 under the pinned LeanLeanBench metric.
